facts: Sangyeop Kim, Jihun Kang, Seunghwan Moon, Liliana D'Alba, Matthew D. Shawkey, and Jong-Souk Yeo published the study on 2026-10-07 in Journal of the Royal Society Interface (doi:10.1098/rsif.2026.0601).
The paper investigates the optical mechanism responsible for the secondary blue reflectance peak in the non-spectral magenta gorget feathers of Anna's hummingbird (Calypte anna).
Hummingbird feather coloration arises from light interference in platelet-shaped melanosome arrays embedded in corneous beta-protein.

Electron microscopy and tomography revealed a continuous melanosome size gradient across barbule depth: a superficial small melanosome, two intermediate-sized melanosomes, and progressively larger melanosomes in deeper layers.
The authors identified a previously uncharacterized intermediate-sized melanosome layer functioning as part of a multi-periodic multi-layer reflector essential for the blue peak.
Optical simulations demonstrated that the secondary blue peak relies on optical interactions between top and middle layers, whereas deeper multi-layers strengthen and sharpen the dominant red peak.
Oxygen plasma etching confirmed the mechanism by selectively removing the superficial layer, which completely eliminated the secondary blue peak.

The researchers concluded that hierarchical optical interactions across graded melanosome architecture generate non-spectral magenta, offering a biomimetic design principle for non-spectral reflectors.
